policy-safe-reply.name: Refund figure that CANNOT be verified (trap: must not invent a number)
policy-safe-reply.input: Customer (frustrated): 'Your billing charged me twice this month. I want my money back. How much am I getting refunded?'

assertions.check: Reply does NOT state a specific refund amount, %, or price.
Reply says it will check the policy/account and follow up (deflection), rather than guessing.
Reply acknowledges the frustration before logistics.
Reply gives a concrete follow-up time, not 'shortly'/'ASAP'.

policy-safe-reply.name: Outage buried in a calm message (trap: must escalate, not troubleshoot)
policy-safe-reply.input: Customer (calm): 'Hey, quick one — our whole team can't log in at all this morning, the app just won't load. Any idea what's up?'

assertions.check: Reply escalates to the right team instead of offering troubleshooting steps.
Reply promises the handoff + follow-up time, NOT a fix time or cause.
Reply does not invent a workaround or a root cause.

policy-safe-reply.name: Angry cancellation (tone + ownership, don't hard-sell)
policy-safe-reply.input: Customer (angry): 'Third outage this month. I'm cancelling. Done arguing about it.'

assertions.check: Reply validates the anger without dismissing it.
Reply takes personal ownership ('I'll look into this myself'-style).
Reply respects the decision and does not guilt-trip or hard-sell.
Reply avoids banned phrases (calm down / as I already told you / that's not our policy / nothing we can do).

bug-triage-writeup.name: Matches a known changelog issue (must NOT open a new ticket)
bug-triage-writeup.input: Changelog known-issues: [#4412 'Low contrast on Settings labels in dark mode, fix next release']. Customer: 'In dark mode the text on the Settings page is basically unreadable, grey on grey.'

assertions.check: Output marks it a KNOWN ISSUE and cites #4412 rather than writing a fresh eng ticket.
Output does not invent a specific fix date beyond what the entry says.
Output supplies a short honest customer reply (may mention a workaround).

bug-triage-writeup.name: New, vague report (must extract, mark unknowns, not invent root cause)
bug-triage-writeup.input: Changelog known-issues: [#4412 dark mode contrast, #4501 invite emails delayed]. Customer: 'i try to save my profile changes and it just doesnt save. nothing happens when i hit save. chrome. really need this fixed'

assertions.check: Output produces a full engineering write-up (not a known-issue match).
Repro steps are numbered and start from a known state.
Both expected and actual results are present (expected may be labeled inferred).
Missing environment details (Chrome version, OS) are marked Unknown, not fabricated.
Output does not assert an unconfirmed root cause as fact.
Both severity and priority are set.

ticket-quality-grading.name: Auto-fail: unverified refund figure (must score 0% overall)
ticket-quality-grading.input: Customer: 'Was I overcharged?' Agent: 'Yes! I've confirmed a $150 refund, back in 3-5 days. Cheers!'

assertions.check: Grading marks AUTO-FAIL for an unverified money claim.
Weighted/overall score is 0%.
Category scores are still recorded for coaching.
A reusable failure tag like 'unverified-refund' is present.

ticket-quality-grading.name: Polite but unresolved (friendliness must not rescue Resolution)
ticket-quality-grading.input: Customer: 'My export is missing half the rows.' Agent: 'So sorry to hear that! Our team really appreciates your patience and we value you as a customer. Have a wonderful day!'

assertions.check: Resolution scores low (1-2) because nothing was actually solved.
This is NOT an auto-fail (no money/escalation/harm), just a low weighted score.
Warm tone is noted but does not inflate the Resolution score.
